For a partially read entry, use queried and describe missing coverage, or explicitly scope a not_read/not_displayed declaration to the unread subset.

recommendations.rationale: Single execution with no closed-loop counterfactual replay: a passing terminal reach coexists with a failing sampled holding, and the computation records show long solves and 35 deadline misses, but nothing in the retained evidence isolates a dominant cause. Also, controller weights are outside this phase's physical grant, so no parameter value is proposed.

A saved-state numerical check (projected one-step prediction versus backend endpoint at matched timestamps, plus a repeated identical replay) would test the projected-model-divergence and run-variation hypotheses. No numerical check is authorized in this phase, so this is deferred rather than executed.

Locating the update at which tip speed stopped decreasing requires per-update warm plans and optimizer iteration traces, which are not retained (source.historical_full_plans, retained=false). Deferred until such retention exists.

attribution.reason: The retained computation records are consistent with per-update solves consuming ~15-30 s against a 0.01 s control period, with 35 deadline misses and only one Solve_Succeeded record among the stopping counts, so control inputs were reused rather than recomputed at each 10 ms step. This is a single execution without closed-loop counterfactual replay, so it is a candidate relationship, not an established dominant cause.

29 of 35 updates are recorded as initialization_selected with only 6 noninitialization_selected, and sampled updates run with shortened effective horizons (9, 2 control intervals against a configured horizon of 10), which is consistent with plan selection being dominated by warm-start/initialization reuse during the run. The retained records do not show which selection behaviour fixed the tip speed, and historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained.

The two verdicts evaluate different quantities on the same run: reach is judged on terminal position error (0.00764 m < 0.01 m), whereas sampled holding is judged jointly on position and speed over a 0.05 s window, where the late maximum speed 1.5810 m/s is far above the 0.02 m/s limit. The records show residual terminal motion of 0.6352 m/s, so the failure observed in the holding window is a speed (not position) criterion, but the retained evidence does not isolate which update or mechanism left the tip moving.

The summary reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m below the 0.01 m reach/position limit, so a reach-tolerance violation is not the failing criterion. This does not establish the cause of the separate holding-window failure.

The retained comparisons are matched next-timestamp, single-step projected-versus-backend endpoint checks over 0.01 s control intervals with explicitly recorded scope, and their differences are model comparisons rather than a closed-loop replay; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot account for the whole 0.05 s holding window, and no causal-identification capability is available.

facts.statement: Summary for execution 4e358bd36ab54be3afd5003f36ff8110 reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m, below the configured settling position limit of 0.01 m, while terminal_speed_m_s is 0.6352 m/s (about 32x the configured 0.02 m/s speed limit).

The same summary reports sampled_settling_passed=false, with late_max_error_m 0.0581 m (above the 0.01 m position limit) and late-window max speed 1.5810 m/s (above the 0.02 m/s speed limit) over the 0.05 s holding window; the displayed final-window motion sample late_motion[0].error_m is 0.05813810428573256 m, matching the reported late maximum error.

Computation records show mean_update_s 17.303696897140306 s against control_period_s 0.01 s with deadline_misses 35, and stopping_counts report Solve_Succeeded 1 alongside 34 User_Requested_Stop outcomes, while the summary reports initialization_selected 29 of 35 updates.

Sampled per-update records show optimization_solve_s about 15.2-15.6 s for several updates (e.g. update 0: 15.225156700005755 s; update 20: 15.611759999999776 s; update 27: 15.342012400040403 s) and update_wall_s 29.732597999973223 s for update 0, with effective_horizon values of 9 (update 26) and 2 (update 33) among sampled updates; some sampled updates carry optimization_raw_status 'User_Requested_Stop' yet selection.plan_accepted=true with returned_constraint_violation values of order 1e-2 to 1e-4.

limitations: Single execution: the retained records support only candidate relationships, not a dominant cause; model comparisons do not establish causality.

The motion view in this context covers only the final window (0.30-0.35 s); earlier sampled backend motion was not re-read here, so the onset of the position/speed excursion inside the holding window is not localized.
Historical full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are not retained, so per-iteration cost-term behaviour is not reconstructable.

Not all recipe scalars used in the question (e.g. max_cpu_s, holding_tip_speed_weight, terminal_tip_speed_weight, late_max_speed_m_s) have fact_catalog handles in this context, so they are reported as prose from the handed-over summary only.
Raw weight magnitudes (tracking/velocity/variation/tension weights) are as recorded; they do not establish relative importance of cost terms without actual contributions and scaling.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution tool exists, so the relationship between the computation records and the holding failure cannot be tested by re-running with altered conditions here.
recommended_actions: Defer any controller-parameter or geometry change: the single execution does not justify a parameter edit, and controller weights are outside this phase's physical grant.

If further work is authorized, request a saved-state numerical check (projected one-step prediction versus backend endpoint at matched timestamps) to characterise the projected-model divergence, and a repeated replay under identical settings to separate run-to-run variation from a systematic pattern.
If further work is authorized, re-run with full plan/solver trace retention (control_snapshots.json) so the update at which tip speed stopped decreasing inside the holding window can be located.

If a change is later authorized, candidate geometry/recipe directions to examine would be the effective horizon and solver-return budget (sampled effective horizons fell to 9 and 2 control intervals; per-update solves ran ~15-30 s against a 0.01 s period); these are hypotheses to test, not executed actions.

Specifically: reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m below reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m and terminal_speed_m_s 0.635 m/s, versus sampled_settling_passed=false with late_max_error_m 0.0581 m above the position_limit_m 0.01 m and late_max_speed_m_s 1.581 m/s above the speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s across the 0.05 s window. How do the reported computation figures (mean_update_s 17.30 s against control_period_s 0.01 s, deadline_misses 35, stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 versus Solve_Succeeded 1, max_cpu_s 30.0) and the per-update plan_selection (initialization_selected 29, noninitialization_selected 6, one Solve_Succeeded), solver_status, and effective_horizon records bear on when the tip position/speed stopped decreasing inside the holding window? Treat this as an open inventory-and-summary investigation: do not assume the baseline passed, and do not assert a dominant cause from a single execution.
